task: Repair the memory endpoint inventory guard without changing runtime behavior
root_cause: The old regular-expression scanner only recognized dictionary returns inside a route's text block. The memory route now returns await engine.manual_compaction.compact(...); that helper still returns ok:false, but the scanner missed it.
rule: Discover response envelopes from function syntax and follow directly returned calls to named same-module functions or explicitly imported source functions. Do not execute application modules or attribute unrelated nested/adjacent function returns to the route.
changes: Added a separate source-only AST scanner used by the inventory guard
Preserved strict checks for unregistered and stale endpoints and disjoint classification tiers
Corrected the memory endpoint's stale client attribution: GUI compact uses /v1/slash; /v1/memory/compact stays registered in NO_UI_CLIENT
Retained the prior removal of the retired local-model endpoint

covered: Direct and asynchronous delegated responses, import aliases and helper chains
Single quotes, nested dictionaries and keyword route paths
Always-success responses and unrelated nested/adjacent functions excluded
Cycles terminate, shadowed imports are not followed and module binding order is respected
Moving a response into a helper preserves discovery; removing its rejection removes discovery
Short history and pending-stop paths preserve runtime state
validation.environment_note: The initial restricted Windows asyncio test stalled in socketpair setup. The same four isolated cases passed with normal process permissions; no live model requests were used.

limits: The scanner follows direct named return calls and absolute from-imports inside the Python source root. It is not a general data-flow or dynamic-dispatch analyzer. No full repository test run was claimed.
